title: How Americans view AI in the workforce: A study
published_window: 2025; within six months before retrieval in the public search result
discussion_signal: The post translates the HBS study into a public-acceptance boundary: support for automating occupations rises from about 30% under current AI capabilities to about 58% when AI is described as outperforming humans at lower cost, while roughly 12% of occupations remain morally off-limits. The post frames the industrial and consumer implication as a distinction between performance concerns that may recede with evidence and human-touch roles where social meaning remains part of the service.
linked_research_question: When US firms introduce AI into industrial or consumer-facing work, which adoption barriers are performance and safety questions, which are durable human-touch boundaries, and who receives the productivity or service-quality gains?
limits: The post is a selected public translation of hypothetical survey judgments, not observed deployment or purchasing behavior
The visible discussion is not a representative sample of US workers, firms, or consumers
The post does not establish actual productivity, job, safety, quality, or trust outcomes
